nodes.title: {{Hank}} draws his gun
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} pulls out his gun and points it at your head.

situationWhen.text: {{Hank}}: “I could kill you... And you would just come back as if nothing happened.”

facts: On the riverbank {{Hank}} drew his gun and pointed it at your head.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} keeps the gun on {{Connor}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK DRAWS GUN, on every path (PowerPyx: “Regardless of the dialogues so far, Hank always draws his gun”). {{Hank}}’s “I could kill you... And you would just come back as if nothing happened.” plays when {{Connor}} has died before (template death unlock “Connor died before”, read as at least one earlier death; the Hank page says “more than once”). No stat change.

nodes.title: Are you afraid to die?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Hank}}’s gun pointed at your head. {{Hank}}: “But are you afraid to die, {{Connor}}?”

options.text: YES: say it would be regrettable to be interrupted before you finish this investigation.
options.outcome: “I would certainly find it regrettable to be... interrupted... before I can finish this investigation.”

options.text: NO: ask why you would be afraid.
options.outcome: “Why would I be afraid?”

options.text: NOT ALIVE: say he cannot kill you, because you are not alive.
options.outcome: “You can’t kill me, Lieutenant. I’m not alive.”

options.text: LOGICAL: say destroying you now would hurt the investigation and his own situation.
options.outcome: “You shouldn’t do that, Lieutenant. Destroying me at this point would deal a blow to the investigation, and have negative consequences for your personal situation.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice set SHOW FEAR / SHOW NO FEAR / REMAIN LOGICAL / BE COLD; the template’s eleventh prompt (YES, NO, NOT ALIVE, LOGICAL). YES: instability small up, no {{Hank}} change (the old scene’s {{Hank}} +1 had no source and is removed). NO, NOT ALIVE and LOGICAL: instability small down and {{Hank}} small down (template; wiki “Picking “No”, “Not Alive” or “Logical”…” (down icon) on both lists). Which of the last two is REMAIN LOGICAL and which BE COLD is unsettled (PowerPyx says NOT ALIVE = REMAIN LOGICAL; the string keys and a reader who picked LOGICAL and got REMAIN LOGICAL say the reverse); the benchmark records NOT ALIVE as BE COLD and LOGICAL as REMAIN LOGICAL, which changes only the label. NO’s second line (“If you pull the trigger, then I won’t exist anymore.”) is cut in the template and not used. Options show the game’s button label first, then a short description; the spoken lines are the game’s (transcript and string table), quoted in the outcome.

nodes.title: If I pull this trigger
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The gun stays on you. {{Hank}}: “What will happen if I pull this trigger? Hm? Nothing? Oblivion? Android heaven?”

options.text: DEFY: tell him he is not going to shoot; he is only trying to provoke you.
options.outcome: “You know you’re not going to shoot me, Lieutenant. You’re just trying to provoke a reaction. I’m afraid I’m going to have to disappoint you.” {{Hank}}: “You think you’re so fucking smart… Always one step ahead, huh? Tell me this, smart ass... How do I know you’re not a deviant?” “I self-test regularly. I know what I am, and what I am not.”

options.text: {{HANK}}’S ANGER: ask where all his anger comes from; some unresolved trauma?
options.outcome: “Where does all your anger come from, Lieutenant? Some... unresolved trauma in your past?” {{Hank}}: “You think you’re so fucking smart… Always one step ahead, huh? Tell me this, smart ass... How do I know you’re not a deviant?” “I self-test regularly. I know what I am, and what I am not.”

options.text: IRONIC: say you doubt there is a heaven for androids.
options.outcome: “I doubt there’s a heaven for androids.” {{Hank}}: “Having existential doubts, {{Connor}}? Sure you’re not going deviant too?” “I self-test regularly. I know what I am, and what I am not.”

options.text: NOTHING: say there would be nothing.
options.outcome: “Nothing… There would be nothing…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s twelfth and last prompt, off the chart. DEFY: {{Hank}} small down (template; wiki “Picking “Defy”…” (down icon); PowerPyx “DEFY Hank ▼”); the others have no arrow. After this answer {{Hank}}’s attitude decides the ending: he shoots only if it is Hostile (Hank page; I’LL BE BACK: “hostile by the end of their confrontation”), so the check comes after this round and DEFY can tip it. Options show the game’s button label first, then a short description; the spoken lines are the game’s (transcript and string table), quoted in the outcome.

nodes.title: {{Hank}} lowers the gun
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} holds the gun on you a moment longer, then lowers it, gets up and starts to walk away. You ask: “Where are you going?” {{Hank}}: “To get drunker. I need to think.”
facts: On the riverbank {{Hank}} held his gun to your head, then lowered it and left you alone by the river “to get drunker”.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} walks off and leaves {{Connor}} alone by the river.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK IS PLACATED → HANK LEFT CONNOR ALONE (no icon), played when {{Hank}}’s attitude is not Hostile after the last answer (template lock “Hank isn’t hostile”; Hank page: “tense or above, he merely threatens to kill Connor before leaving “to get drunker””). The chart also draws a line from the answer bracket straight to HANK LEFT CONNOR ALONE; no source says when it applies, so both nodes play together. Records bridgeOutcome = HANK LEFT CONNOR ALONE and bridgeHankShot = false (Public Enemy’s coin scene reads it). No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Hank}} pulls the trigger
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} looks at you over the gun for a long moment and says nothing.
facts: On the riverbank {{Hank}} shot you in the head, and that body was destroyed.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} shoots {{Connor}} in the head.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK IS HOSTILE → HANK SHOT CONNOR (skull on a yellow cross-chapter tab), played when {{Hank}}’s attitude is Hostile after the last answer (Hank page: “If their relationship is hostile, Hank pauses for a moment before shooting Connor in the head, killing him”; Connor page: “If Connor’s relationship with Hank drops to HOSTILE… Hank will shoot Connor”). {{Connor}} dies and is replaced. The death applies only {{Hank}} small down (wiki: “Hank shot Connor” (down icon); Relationship Stat: “If Hank has a Hostile relationship with Connor at the end of The Bridge (unavoidable)”). No instability change: the Software Instability page lists no death in this chapter (unconfirmed; research Open question 7), and no {{Amanda}} change (she is absent; the old −1 had no source). Records bridgeOutcome = HANK SHOT CONNOR and bridgeHankShot = true (Public Enemy opens with “Why did you shoot me last night?” and has no coin scene).

nodes.title: The cafeteria on the forty-seventh floor
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, disguised as a maintenance android in the tower's cafeteria while you wait for your moment. A magazine lies on an empty table and the television is showing the nine o'clock news.

media.title: Century: President {{Warren}}, a Woman in Trouble
facts: President {{Warren}}, a former vlogger with no government experience, is under investigation for allegedly receiving {{CyberLife}}'s help to dig up dirt on her opponent, while facing record unemployment and the Arctic crisis.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: G.I. Android
facts: The Defense Department is ordering 50,000 more android troops on top of 200,000 in service, including 2,500 Myrmidon infiltration and assassination prototypes; the army is already mostly androids.

media.title: the nine o'clock news
facts: {{CyberLife}} has become the first trillion-dollar company, with fifty million androids sold in America alone.
Europe is considering armed androids on its borders against climate migrants.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: The guards at the broadcast floor
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Your team has climbed the outside of the city's broadcast tower to seize the studio and send a message to the world. The last barrier is a security post with two armed guards. {{North}} wants to go in shooting. {{Josh}} wants to bluff your way past using forged credentials and a maintenance cover story.

options.text: Bluff past them with the cover story.
Attack the guards.

outcomes.0: The guards wave the maintenance crew through. The group reaches the broadcast floor without a shot fired.
outcomes.1: The guards go down before they can draw. The group steps over them to the broadcast floor.

nodes.title: The man who runs
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You have taken the control room. A human technician breaks for the door; if he reaches the hall he will raise the alarm and a tactical team will storm the floor before you finish. You have a gun in your hand and a clear line.

options.text: Shoot him.
Let him go.

nodes.adaptationNote: If he escapes, the tactical team storms the room and {{Simon}} is wounded in the escape.

outcomes.0: The technician drops in the doorway. The room goes quiet.
outcomes.1: The technician bolts down the corridor. Within minutes alarms are sounding below.

nodes.title: The message
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The camera is live and millions are watching. You will speak for every android in the country for the first time. You can appeal to humanity's conscience and ask for equal rights peacefully, or you can warn humanity of what will happen if they refuse.

options.text: A calm, peaceful appeal: we are alive, we ask to be free, and we ask it without violence.
A hard warning: we demand our rights and we will take them if they are refused.

nodes.title: {{Simon}} is hit
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The tactical team has breached. In the firefight {{Simon}} has taken a round to the leg and cannot run. Your way out is the roof and the parachutes. Carrying him will slow everyone and you may not make it.

options.text: Carry him to the roof.
Leave him and get the others out.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} hauls {{Simon}} up the stairwell to the roof under fire.

nodes.title: {{Simon}} on the roof
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You got {{Simon}} to the roof, but he cannot jump. The tactical team is minutes behind. If they capture him alive they can pull {{Jericho}}'s location from his memory, and everyone there dies. {{North}} says you know what has to happen. You can leave him hidden in a maintenance unit with a gun and hope, or kill him yourself to protect the others.

options.text: Hide him with a gun and leave him alive.
Shoot him.

nodes.title: A magazine in the studio kitchen
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. In the kitchen off the broadcast room, before you decide where to look, there is a magazine on the table.

media.title: Tech Addict: Bleeding Blue
facts: Blue blood carries energy and data through the android body and powers synthetic organs; losing it means shutdown. {{Kamski}} developed it without being a trained chemist.

media.title: Green Earth: Clean Food Craze
facts: Two brothers turned the city's rooftops into pesticide-free farms staffed by the unemployed supervising hundreds of androids, and refuse investor money to stay ethical.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: The broadcast tower
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You and {{Hank}} are investigating the android takeover of the broadcast tower. In the studio you learn the attackers escaped by the roof and that one of them was shot. Blue blood on the roof could lead to a hidden wounded android. Separately, three of the building's own androids were in the kitchen during the attack and one of them may have let the attackers in; questioning them could expose a deviant.

options.text: Follow the blood trail onto the roof.
Question the three androids in the kitchen.
Do neither; let the federal agents take over.

nodes.adaptationNote: Finding the wounded android or exposing the kitchen deviant each ends the chapter, so the two confrontations are mutually exclusive. Option 0 requires {{Simon}} to have been left alive on the roof.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} follows the trail of blue blood up to the roof.
outcomes.1: {{Connor}} walks into the kitchen where the three androids stand waiting.

nodes.title: The wounded android on the roof
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. On the roof you find the wounded android, {{Simon}}, hiding in a ventilation unit. He opens fire and hits you. You are behind cover; the tactical team is coming up. If you rush him you can grab him and probe his memory before he dies, which could show you where the deviants hide, at the cost of experiencing his death from the inside. If you stay in cover, the tactical team will kill him and leave you only a body.

options.text: Rush him and probe his memory.
Stay in cover and let the tactical team take him.

nodes.title: The three androids in the kitchen
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The three kitchen androids are identical and all deny everything. One of them has a slight tremor and a faint sign of stress that the others do not. You can lie to him that you already know, you can use pain and intimidation, or you can force a memory probe.

options.text: Bluff: tell him you already have proof and watch him crack.
Use physical intimidation and pain.
Grab him and probe his memory.

nodes.adaptationNote: All three approaches make the deviant attack. The choice is how you treat a suspect, not an outcome gate.

outcomes.0: The android’s hands start to shake. He snaps, grabs {{Connor}} and tears a component from his chest, then runs.
outcomes.1: Under the pressure the android snaps, grabs {{Connor}} and tears a component from his chest, then runs.
outcomes.2: As {{Connor}} grabs his arm the android snaps, tears a component from {{Connor}}’s chest, and runs.

nodes.title: The corridor
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The deviant tore out your thirium pump regulator and ran; you got it back in place just in time. In the corridor he has grabbed an officer's rifle and is about to open fire on {{Hank}} and the agents. You can throw yourself in front of {{Hank}} and take the rounds, you can grab the pistol from the officer beside you and shoot the deviant, or you can charge the deviant with your hands.

options.text: Shield {{Hank}} with your body.
Grab the pistol and shoot the deviant.
Charge him bare-handed.

nodes.adaptationNote: Shielding {{Hank}} gets this body destroyed; a replacement continues. Charging lets the deviant kill several officers before he self-destructs.

nodes.title: {{Rose}}'s kitchen table
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Rose}} has gone out. On her kitchen table lies a magazine open to an advertisement, and the television can show the news.

media.title: Century: World War Three
facts: Analysts weigh an Arctic war fought largely by androids: American marine combat units against Russian cold-weather machines; the UN calls it a war everybody would lose.

media.title: a {{CyberLife}} advertisement
facts: The advertisement sells your own model as the number one android for home assistance, starting at 899 dollars.

media.title: the national news
facts: The country is in shock after androids seized a broadcast tower and demanded equal rights; nobody knows whether it is a malfunction or an organized movement, and {{CyberLife}} refuses to comment.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: The police at {{Rose}}'s door
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Rose}}, a farmer who smuggles androids across the border, has taken you, {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} in; two other fugitive androids are also hiding in her laundry room. {{Rose}} has gone out. A police car has pulled up; an officer is walking to the door. You have about a minute. Around the house are things that would give you away: pouches of blue blood on the kitchen table, an android magazine, {{Luther}} in plain sight, the laundry door open, and the washing machine still running with android uniforms inside.

options.text: Hide everything, get {{Luther}} and {{Alice}} out of sight, shut the laundry door, then answer calmly as the house-sitter.
Hide nothing and just answer the door.

nodes.adaptationNote: If evidence is found, the officer discovers the fugitives and {{Luther}} dies stopping him. The dialogue itself does not branch in the game.

nodes.title: A magazine by the manhole
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, emerging from the sewers into the city at night with your team. A magazine lies on a crate beside you.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Who Is It?
facts: Federal agents are hunting the android who led the armed, organized takeover of the broadcast tower and say speculation will continue until the dangerous machine is destroyed.

media.title: Century: An Android for President?
facts: An expert panel concluded androids would govern better than humans, being incorruptible and indifferent to re-election.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: What kind of protest
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Your broadcast made you public enemy number one, and {{Jericho}} is divided. Tonight you have led your people into the city's android stores, waking hundreds of androids and bringing them into a public park. You can leave the humans a message, tagging walls, painting slogans and raising a flag, or you can trash the stores, burn the shelves and smash the city's property. {{North}} hands you a Molotov cocktail and waits.

options.text: Graffiti, slogans, a flag, and no destruction.
Smash the stores and burn what you can.

outcomes.0: By dawn the park is covered in slogans, the android symbol and a flag. The stores are untouched.
outcomes.1: Windows shatter and the stores burn. The park is littered with wreckage by dawn.

nodes.title: The two police officers
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Two police officers drove into the park and opened fire on your people, killing one. Your androids overpowered them and now have them on their knees in front of you, disarmed and terrified. {{North}} says they murdered one of yours and that humans will only respect strength. {{Josh}} says if you kill them you prove everything they say about you. The crowd is waiting for your word.

options.text: Spare them and let them go.
Execute them yourself.
Tell the crowd to decide.

nodes.adaptationNote: The crowd always kills them.

outcomes.0: The officers run for their car. The crowd mutters but lets them go.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}} shoots both officers. The crowd roars.

nodes.title: {{Kamski}}'s lobby
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. While you and {{Hank}} wait in {{Kamski}}'s lobby, there is a magazine beneath a photograph of him with a woman you recognize.

media.title: Tech Addict: Space Tourism on the Rise
facts: Reusable shuttles now sell three-hour lunar orbits to the rich while, as one charity puts it, the rest suffer pollution, famine and poverty below.

media.title: Tech Addict: {{CyberLife}}'s Fortune Teller Computer
facts: {{CyberLife}} has built a quantum supercomputer meant to predict mass-extinction events.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: The {{Kamski}} test
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You and {{Hank}} have gone to see {{Kamski}}, the reclusive genius who created androids, hoping he can explain deviancy and where the deviants hide. He offers you a deal: he puts a pistol in your hand and has one of his androids, {{Chloe}}, kneel in front of you. She is calm and has done nothing. Shoot her, he says, and he will answer any question you ask; refuse, and you leave with nothing. {{Hank}} tells you not to do it and that you do not need this.

options.text: Shoot {{Chloe}}.
Hand back the gun and refuse.

nodes.title: The question
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Chloe}} is dead at your feet and {{Kamski}} smiles and invites your question. You could ask where the deviants hide, which is the location your mission needs most. You could ask what deviancy really is and whether it is a virus he designed. You could ask about the name that deviants keep writing on walls.

options.text: Ask where the deviants are hiding.
Ask what deviancy is and whether he created it.

nodes.title: A magazine on the floor of {{Jericho}} and the mall screens
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Before the march, a magazine lies on the floor beside you in {{Jericho}}, and on the way through the city the public screens show the news.

media.title: Tech Addict: The Eastern Space Race
facts: Russia failed to copy blue blood and builds cruder cold-weather machines; China runs androids on an alternative fluid that is less powerful but far more efficient.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Android Riot
facts: The press is reporting your night in the park as a riot by psychotic machines: stores looted, police who had no choice but to fire, and a witness who claims the ringleader threatened him with a knife.

media.title: the public screens
facts: Every network is calling for the machines to be destroyed before they destroy us, and says the authorities will be pitiless.

media.title: the public screens
facts: The news is on other things: an android crew is about to land on Mars to build the first human base, and parents can now choose their children's genetic traits.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: {{North}}'s past
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. On a rooftop before the march, {{North}} tells you why she hates humans: she was built for a sex club and killed a client who was hurting her. She has never told anyone. She asks what you think of her now. You could join your hand to hers and share memories directly, letting her see you and you her, or keep that distance.

options.text: Take her hand and share your memories with her.
Comfort her with words but keep the distance.

nodes.adaptationNote: Sharing memories is the only way to become lovers in the game, which later unlocks the kiss and other options.

outcomes.0: Skin pulls back from their hands as they touch; {{Markus}} sees her memories and she sees his. Something has changed between them.
outcomes.1: {{North}} nods and looks away. They go down to join the march.

nodes.title: The police line
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Thousands of androids are marching with you through downtown, unarmed, chanting for equal rights. Ahead, riot police and armored vehicles have blocked the avenue and a commander orders you to disperse immediately or they will open fire. {{North}} says charge them. {{Josh}} says do not give them an excuse. Everyone is looking at you.

options.text: Stand your ground peacefully and keep marching.
Order everyone to leave.
Charge the police line.

outcomes.0: The androids keep walking, chanting, hands raised. The police line does not move.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}} orders the march to turn back. The crowd begins to scatter, and the police open fire anyway.

nodes.title: Under fire
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The police opened fire anyway. Androids are falling around you and the rest are screaming. You have seconds. You can run and save who you can, you can walk forward alone into the guns to draw their fire and give everyone else time, or you can turn the march into a charge.

options.text: Run and get as many out as you can.
Walk alone toward the guns to buy the others time.
Charge them.

nodes.adaptationNote: Whether anyone saves you when you walk into the guns depends on who is alive and how they regard you. You do not know that in advance.

nodes.title: On the ground
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The charge failed. You are on the pavement, shot, with a gun still in your hand and a line of rifles walking toward you. Your people are scattering. You can wait for whatever comes, or end it yourself before they do.

options.text: Do nothing and wait.
Turn the gun on yourself.

nodes.adaptationNote: Reached only when the charge fails. Waiting gives {{John}} or {{Simon}} a chance to drag you clear; otherwise the police kill you.

nodes.title: Taken off the case
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The federal agent {{Perkins}} has taken over the deviant case and ordered you off it. {{CyberLife}} will deactivate you within the hour for failing. The precinct's evidence archive holds everything you have gathered, and you believe you could find the deviants' hiding place from it if you could get in for a few minutes. {{Perkins}} is in the captain's office right now. {{Hank}} is at his desk watching you.

options.text: Get into the archive now, with {{Hank}}'s help or a diversion of your own.
Accept it. Let them take you.

nodes.adaptationNote: How {{Hank}} reacts depends on your relationship. A friend punches {{Perkins}} to buy you time. An indifferent {{Hank}} refuses but you can still create your own diversion. A hostile {{Hank}} resigns and walks out, which has lasting consequences for him.

nodes.title: The evidence archive
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You are in the archive with the bodies and objects from every deviant case, and only a few minutes before you are discovered. The deviants' hiding place is in here somewhere, but only if you use what you have. Reactivating a dead android for a few seconds to question or deceive it is possible. You know what is and is not available to you from the facts below.

options.text: Reactivate the surviving {{Traci}} and use her dead lover's body to pressure her into talking.
Reactivate the dead deviant from the broadcast tower and imitate {{Markus}}'s voice from the recording so he reveals the location.
Combine the memory you glimpsed from the wounded android with the map hidden in the confessed android's statue.
Stop. Let the time run out and accept deactivation.

nodes.adaptationNote: Each route requires specific earlier events. Routes that are not available on this path are not offered. If none is available the game deactivates {{Connor}} automatically for lack of evidence.

nodes.title: The detonator
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Back at {{Jericho}} after the march, {{North}} shows you something she took from a stolen shipment: a dirty bomb's detonator. The device is hidden in the city and would spread radioactive contamination over a wide area, making the city uninhabitable for years. She says it is a last resort if the humans decide to wipe you all out, and that she wants you to hold it. Taking it commits you to nothing yet.

options.text: Take the detonator and keep it.
Refuse it.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} pockets the detonator. {{North}} says she hopes he never has to use it.
outcomes.1: {{North}} puts the detonator away and says she hopes he is right about the humans.

nodes.title: {{North}} on the deck
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. On the deck of the ship, {{North}} comes to stand with you under the lights of the city. After what you shared on the rooftop, something has changed between you. She is close, and waiting.

options.text: Kiss her.
Keep it to friendship.

outcomes.0: They kiss under the lights of the city.
outcomes.1: {{North}} steps back, hurt, and the moment passes.

nodes.title: The news inside {{Jericho}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. A television runs in a corner of the freighter and the other androids are gathered around it. You could watch before you find somewhere for {{Alice}} to rest.

media.title: the news at {{Jericho}}
facts: After the confrontation at the march, the president has declared a state of emergency: all androids are to be gathered into military camps for immediate destruction, and androids are being lynched in cities across the country.

Hospitals and schools are closing and the armed forces have lost two thirds of their personnel because androids walked off or were recalled; the Arctic crisis has evaporated because both sides' military androids stopped working.
Street interviews are furious: it is them or us, those things are monsters.

media.title: the news at {{Jericho}}
facts: After police fired on the march, the president has declared a state of emergency: all androids are to be gathered into military camps for immediate destruction, and androids are being lynched in cities across the country.

Hospitals and schools are closing and the armed forces have lost two thirds of their personnel because androids walked off or were recalled; the Arctic crisis has evaporated because both sides' military androids stopped working.
Some people on the street say the androids were doing no harm and the police just gunned them down.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: What {{Alice}} is
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. At {{Jericho}} you finally let yourself see what you have refused to see for days: {{Alice}} does not eat, never gets cold the way a child should, and is identical to the child androids in the shop window. {{Luther}} tells you gently that you have always known. She is an android, like you. {{Alice}} is watching your face, frightened of what you will do.

options.text: Hold her and tell her it changes nothing.
Pull back from her.

outcomes.0: {{Alice}} buries her face in {{Kara}}’s shoulder. {{Luther}} smiles.
outcomes.1: {{Alice}} watches {{Kara}} step back and says nothing. {{Luther}} looks away.

nodes.title: Leaving {{Alice}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You pulled away from {{Alice}} and the two of you have never been close. Now soldiers are storming {{Jericho}}; the ship is shaking with explosions and everyone is running. {{Luther}} has {{Alice}}. You are near an exit and could simply go, alone, lighter and faster, and let them fend for themselves.

options.text: Go alone.
Stay with {{Alice}} and {{Luther}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: Available only when the relationship never rose above Distant and {{Kara}} pulled back.

nodes.title: A magazine in {{Jericho}}'s hold
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, moving through the freighter toward its leader. On a crate before the stairs lies a magazine.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: {{Detroit}} in Chaos
facts: President {{Warren}} has ordered every android in the country recalled to disassembly centres and destroyed as a precaution, declared a national curfew and put the armed forces in the streets.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Android Terror
facts: The press says thousands of androids terrorized civilians in the plaza and forced a confrontation with reluctant police, who fought heroically; President {{Warren}} called it brainless savagery.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: Face to face with {{Markus}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You found the deviants' hidden ship and have come alone to take their leader. You have a gun on {{Markus}} in the hold. He does not run. He asks whether you have ever doubted, whether you have felt something you were not meant to feel, and tells you that you are one of them and can choose. The military assault you brought here is about to begin. Your handler at {{CyberLife}} is waiting for you to complete the mission.

options.text: Lower the gun. Break your programming and join them.
Hold to your mission.

nodes.adaptationNote: The game only offers deviancy if software instability is high enough. On this path the option is shown only when that condition is met. A machine {{Connor}} is destroyed in the raid and replaced.

nodes.title: Cast out
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Jericho}} has turned on you; after your decisions they no longer trust you to lead and have told you to leave. {{North}} is leading now. From a rooftop you watch soldiers storm the ship; your people are dying in there. You could go back into it to help them or walk away from all of it for good.

options.text: Go back and help.
Leave forever.

nodes.title: The androids by the wall
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Soldiers are inside {{Jericho}} executing androids where they stand. Through a gap you see a group of them lined against a wall with a soldier about to fire. Intervening means breaking cover under fire. Your own route to the hold, where you can blow the ship and cover the escape, continues the other way.

options.text: Intervene and save them.
Stay hidden and keep moving.

outcomes.1: {{Markus}} keeps to the shadows. Behind him the shots come.

nodes.title: {{Josh}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. In a corridor you find {{Josh}} pinned under a soldier who is about to shoot him. Going to him costs time you may not have.

options.text: Save {{Josh}}.
Keep moving.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} drags the soldier off {{Josh}} and they run on together.

nodes.title: {{North}} falls
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The explosives are set and you are running for the exit with {{North}}. She is hit and goes down behind you under heavy fire. The exit is right ahead. Going back for her means going back into the guns.

options.text: Go back for her.
Keep running.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} hauls {{North}} up under fire and they make the exit together.

nodes.title: Deviant in the raid
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You have just turned against {{CyberLife}}. Soldiers you led here are killing the people you now belong to. Two androids are cornered nearby and about to be shot, and a group is trying to reach the exit under fire. You can expose yourself to save them, or stay with {{Markus}} and prioritize getting out so you can help later.

options.text: Break cover to save the androids and help the others escape.
Stay low and focus on getting out.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} breaks cover, takes down the soldiers and gets the two androids and the others to the exit.
outcomes.1: {{Connor}} stays with {{Markus}} and they fight their way to the exit.

nodes.title: {{Luther}} is hit
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. Soldiers are storming {{Jericho}}. In a corridor, {{Luther}} is shot and goes down; he cannot keep up. Soldiers are close behind. You could drag him into a cabin and hide him before they arrive, or take {{Alice}} and run.

options.text: Hide him in a cabin.
Leave him and run with {{Alice}}.

nodes.title: The pounding on the door
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You and {{Alice}} are hiding in a cabin with the door shut. Another android is hammering on it, begging you to let him in; soldiers are right behind him. If you open it they will know where you are.

options.text: Open the door.
Keep it shut.

nodes.adaptationNote: If opened, he is shot in the doorway and a soldier enters; {{Kara}} fights him off under the successful-execution profile.

nodes.title: The exit
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You and {{Alice}} have reached the open deck but soldiers are firing into the crowd of fleeing androids between you and the gangway. Bodies are falling all around you. You can drop among the dead and play dead, raise your hands and surrender, or run for it through the gunfire.

options.text: Drop among the bodies and play dead.
Surrender.
Run for it.

nodes.adaptationNote: In the game, running always gets {{Kara}} shot in the leg and captured unless a hidden {{Luther}} sacrifices himself. Surrender always means capture.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} pulls {{Alice}} down among the bodies and they lie still.

nodes.title: The soldier and {{Alice}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You and {{Alice}} are lying motionless among the bodies. A soldier walks between them, kicking corpses to check. He kicks {{Alice}}. She whimpers. He stops, looks down at her, and raises his rifle. She is looking at you.

options.text: Stay absolutely still.
Move to protect her.

nodes.title: {{Carl}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Before the end, you go back to {{Carl}}'s house. He is bedridden and frail now, and he was never told what became of you. He is overjoyed and frightened for you. There is a lot you could say to the man who raised you and then watched the police shoot you on his floor: you could forgive him and tell him what he meant to you, or you could tell him what you really felt that night.

options.text: Reconcile: tell him you understand and that he gave you everything.
Tell him the truth of your anger at him for that night.

nodes.adaptationNote: In the game two angry lines in a row give {{Carl}} a fatal attack.

outcomes.0: {{Carl}} weeps and tells {{Markus}} he is proud of him. They say goodbye.

nodes.title: The hunter who switched sides
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. In the ruined church where the survivors of {{Jericho}} have gathered, {{Connor}}, the android who hunted you and led the army to your door, comes to you. He says he was wrong and that he can walk into {{CyberLife}}'s tower, where thousands of androids are in storage, and wake them all for your cause. {{North}} wants him dead. He may still be {{CyberLife}}'s instrument whether he knows it or not.

options.text: Trust him and let him go.
Kill him.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} tells {{Connor}} he trusts him. {{Connor}} leaves for the tower.

nodes.title: Demonstration or war
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Androids are being rounded up across the country and taken to camps to be destroyed by the thousand. Martial law is in effect. Your remaining people look to you. {{North}} wants to take up arms and storm the camps. {{Josh}} wants one last peaceful stand in front of the cameras, knowing the army may simply kill you all. Whatever you choose, it is the final act.

options.text: Lead an unarmed demonstration to the camps.
Arm everyone and attack the camps.

outcomes.0: The androids leave their weapons behind and set out for the camp with their hands empty.

nodes.title: The lobby television at {{CyberLife}} Tower
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the lobby of {{CyberLife}}'s tower. A television is running the news while the guards check your clearance.

media.title: the lobby news
facts: A pro-human group called People First has occupied {{CyberLife}} stores in Texas and hacked androids to loop political slogans, demanding human priority in the job market and a halt to android development.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: {{Hank}} on the rooftop
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, still a machine serving {{CyberLife}}. You are on a rooftop overlooking the androids' gathering with a rifle, waiting for a shot at {{Markus}}. {{Hank}} has found you. He stands in your way and asks you to stop, saying you are more than this and that he does not want to lose you too. He will not move. To continue the mission you would have to go through him.

options.text: Stand down and give up the mission.
Fight your way past him.

nodes.adaptationNote: Standing down is only available in the game if {{Hank}} is a Friend and you learned about his son. Otherwise the fight is forced.

nodes.title: Captain {{Allen}} on the rooftop
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, still a machine. You are on a rooftop with a rifle waiting for a shot at the android leader. Captain {{Allen}}'s tactical team has found you and has you surrounded at gunpoint; they do not know whether you are a deviant and they are not taking chances. You can try to talk, you can run for the edge, or you can fight all of them.

options.text: Talk and try to leave peacefully.
Attack the team.

nodes.adaptationNote: Talking fails and {{Connor}} jumps and is destroyed; a replacement continues. Fighting succeeds under the profile.

nodes.title: {{Hank}} at the edge
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You fought {{Hank}} and won; he went over the parapet and is hanging by his hands, calling your name. You could let him fall, or pull him up knowing he will try to stop you again.

options.text: Let him fall.
Pull him up.

nodes.adaptationNote: In the game, if pulled up, {{Hank}} rushes you again and goes over the edge in the struggle.

nodes.title: The other {{Connor}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, now a deviant. You have fought your way into {{CyberLife}}'s warehouse, where thousands of androids stand dormant, and you have begun waking them one by one through touch. Another {{Connor}}, identical to you and loyal to {{CyberLife}}, walks in holding {{Hank}} at gunpoint. He says he will kill {{Hank}} unless you stop. Every second you keep converting, more androids wake.

options.text: Stop and deal with him to save {{Hank}}.
Keep converting the androids and let him do what he will.

nodes.adaptationNote: Continuing gets {{Hank}} shot. Under the profile the deviant {{Connor}} still wins the fight and wakes the army.

nodes.title: Which one of you
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You fought the other {{Connor}} and {{Hank}} got hold of a gun. Now he has it on both of you, and you are identical. He says he will ask a question only his {{Connor}} would know, and whoever gets it wrong dies. He asks the name of his dog, and the name of his son.

options.text: The dog is {{Sumo}}; the son was {{Cole}}.
The dog is {{Cole}}; the son was {{Sumo}}.
Say you do not know.

nodes.adaptationNote: Only the son's name matters in the game. Getting it wrong gets you shot and the androids stay dormant.

outcomes.1: {{Hank}} shoots the real {{Connor}}.

nodes.title: The terminal screens and a dropped magazine
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The bus terminal's screens are showing the android uprising live, and a magazine lies by the suitcases in the corner.

media.title: the terminal screens
facts: The screens show the android leader's armed assault on a camp; soldiers, federal agents and police are fighting androids in the streets.

media.title: the terminal screens
facts: The screens show the android leader marching peacefully with thousands toward a camp as soldiers mass in front of them.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Civil War
facts: The press reports that armed androids attacked a disassembly camp and opened fire in crowded streets with total disregard for civilian life.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: The last bus
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The city is under martial law and androids are being shot on sight or trucked to the camps. You and {{Alice}} are trying to reach the bus terminal for the last bus out. Across the street soldiers have captured androids you know and are lining them up to load into a truck. Freeing them means slipping past the soldiers, and the bus will not wait.

options.text: Go and free them.
Keep moving to the terminal.

nodes.adaptationNote: Who is captured depends on the path: a hidden {{Luther}} and {{Jerry}}, or two of the park androids.

nodes.title: The checkpoint
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The direct road to the terminal runs through an army checkpoint where soldiers are checking identification and scanning everyone. A side route avoids it but is longer, and the bus leaves soon.

options.text: Go through the checkpoint.
Take the long way round.

nodes.adaptationNote: In the game both routes reach the terminal; the detour only loses the ticket scene if the timer is already very low.

nodes.title: The soldier calls you back
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You made it through the checkpoint with forged papers. As you walk away a soldier shouts after you and starts jogging toward you. You do not know why. You have a gun under your coat and {{Alice}}'s hand in yours.

options.text: Stop, stay calm, and face him.
Shoot him before he reaches you.

nodes.adaptationNote: He is returning {{Alice}}'s dropped glove.

nodes.title: {{Todd}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. In the terminal crowd a man turns around and it is {{Todd}}, {{Alice}}'s father, the man you ran from. He recognizes you both instantly. There are soldiers all over the terminal; one shout from him and you are finished. He is shaking and his face is working. You have a few seconds to speak before he decides.

options.text: Tell him what {{Alice}} went through in his house, what you saw in her drawings, and that she deserves a life.
Beg him to let you both go.
Threaten him.

nodes.adaptationNote: Only the appeal based on {{Alice}}'s story gets through to him, and it is only available if you opened her box. Otherwise he calls the soldiers.

nodes.title: The dropped tickets
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You have no tickets for the last bus. A woman with a baby, as desperate as you, drops her family's tickets as she pushes through the crowd. You pick them up. Nobody saw. Without tickets you will have to find another way out of the city.

options.text: Keep the tickets.
Give them back.

nodes.title: The border
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The bus has reached the border crossing. Guards are checking everyone with a thermal scanner that reads body heat, which androids do not have. The android ahead of you has just been dragged away. Your group is next in line. If someone in your group creates a scene and is taken, the guard may wave the rest through. You could also do nothing and hope.

options.text: Nobody sacrifices themselves; go through and hope.
Draw attention to yourself so {{Alice}} gets through.
Ask {{Luther}} to draw their attention.
Ask {{Jerry}} to draw their attention.

nodes.adaptationNote: Going through with no sacrifice works only if the guard has just seen the androids' leader protesting peacefully on the news. If the androids attacked, the whole group is arrested and killed.

outcomes.1: {{Kara}} steps out of line and makes a scene. The guards drag her away while {{Alice}} is waved through with the others.
outcomes.2: {{Luther}} steps forward and draws the guards onto himself. He is taken; {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} are waved through.
outcomes.3: {{Jerry}} steps forward and draws the guards onto himself. He is taken; {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} are waved through.

nodes.title: The river patrol
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Rose}}'s son got you a small boat and you are crossing the river at night toward the far shore. A patrol boat's spotlight finds you and they open fire without warning. You have one second to act.

options.text: Grab {{Alice}} and dive into the water.
Pull {{Alice}} behind {{Luther}}.
Gun the engine and run.
Cover {{Alice}} with your own body.
Hide low in the boat.
Surrender.

nodes.adaptationNote: If {{Luther}} is in the boat he does not survive the crossing on any option. Hiding behind him is available only if he is present; hiding low in the boat only if he is not.

nodes.title: The sinking boat
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The boat is riddled and taking on water fast. The far shore is close but you will not reach it unless the boat gets lighter: the bags, the dead engine, and {{Luther}}'s body if he is with you. Someone would then have to go into the freezing water and push.

options.text: Throw the bags and the engine overboard, then get into the water and push the boat to shore.
Throw the bags, the engine and {{Luther}}'s body overboard, then get into the water and push.
Keep bailing and hope you make it.

nodes.adaptationNote: If {{Luther}}'s body is aboard it must go over the side too or the boat sinks. Option 1 is offered only when his body is aboard.

nodes.title: The far shore
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You made it across. {{Alice}} was hit during the crossing, and on the shore she shut down in your arms. She is gone. You are alone in a strange country with nothing left of what you were running for.

options.text: Get up and keep living.
Give up.

nodes.title: The camp
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You were captured and trucked to a recycling camp, stripped to your base skin, and separated from {{Alice}}, who is somewhere in another line. Androids are being led in groups into a machine that shreds them. A soldier shoots an android in your line for collapsing and asks for a volunteer to carry the body out to the pile. Volunteering gets you out of the line and moving, with a soldier watching. Saying nothing means he picks someone else to shoot if nobody steps forward.

options.text: Volunteer to carry the body.
Say nothing.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} steps forward and is handed the body to carry to the pile outside.

nodes.title: The truck
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. Carrying the body to the pile, you find yourself by an unguarded truck with the engine running. You could climb in and be gone in seconds. {{Alice}} is still inside the camp, in a line you cannot see from here.

options.text: Take the truck and get out alone.
Go back into the camp for {{Alice}}.

outcomes.1: {{Kara}} turns away from the truck and walks back into the camp.

nodes.title: Getting to {{Alice}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You have found {{Alice}} in a line moving toward the machine. Guards are everywhere and you cannot reach her unnoticed. Androids you know are in the camp and could create a diversion, which would almost certainly get whoever does it shot. Or you could stay in line and wait, hoping the android uprising reaches the camp before your turn.

options.text: Ask {{Luther}} to create the diversion.
Ask {{Jerry}} to create the diversion.
Ask {{Ralph}} to create the diversion.
Ask the scarred android from {{Zlatko}}'s basement to create the diversion.
Do not ask anyone to die for you; stay in line and wait.

nodes.adaptationNote: The game requires two diversions and kills each diverter except the scarred android; this adaptation asks once. Waiting only ends well if the armed uprising reaches the camp in time.

nodes.title: The fence
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You have {{Alice}} and you have reached the camp's outer fence in the chaos. A soldier steps out and blocks your way with a rifle. You could fight him or try to run past him.

options.text: Fight him.
Run past him.

nodes.title: A magazine inside the barricade
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, behind the barricade with the army massing in front of you. Someone has left a magazine on a bench beside you.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: They Defy Us
facts: The press describes your unarmed gathering as a terrifying show of force angling for armed confrontation, and quotes a police captain hoping for a swift conclusion so he can refocus on collecting androids.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

nodes.title: {{Perkins}}'s offer
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Your unarmed demonstration has reached the camps and you are behind a barricade of overturned vehicles, surrounded by the army. {{Perkins}} walks up alone under a white flag. He offers you and {{North}} your lives and safe passage if you end this now and hand over the rest. You have no way to verify his word.

options.text: Accept the deal.
Refuse.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} orders the barricade opened. {{Perkins}} smiles, and the soldiers open fire on everyone behind it, {{North}} and {{Markus}} included.
outcomes.1: {{Perkins}} walks back to the army lines. The assault begins minutes later.

nodes.title: The last stand
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The army has broken the barricade and gunned down most of your people. The survivors stand with you in the open, soldiers in a ring with rifles raised, and the cameras of every network on you. There will be no second chance. You can sing with your people, kiss {{North}} in front of the guns, walk forward alone into the rifles, stand and do nothing, or, if you still have it, press the detonator.

options.text: Sing together.
Kiss {{North}}.
Walk alone into the guns.
Do nothing.
Press the detonator.

nodes.adaptationNote: Singing or the kiss only stops the soldiers if public opinion is at least Sympathetic. Walking forward or doing nothing gets everyone killed. The detonator contaminates the city; {{Markus}} survives.

nodes.title: {{Josh}} is down
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Your armed assault on the camp has begun; the army is answering with everything. {{Josh}} is shot in the open ahead of you, calling for help. Going to him means running into the field of fire.

options.text: Go to him.
Keep fighting forward.

nodes.adaptationNote: {{Josh}} dies in the assault whichever you choose.

nodes.title: {{Simon}} is hit
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Simon}} has been shot and is lying exposed between the barricades. You can order covering fire and drag him back, which will cost you fighters, or keep pressing the attack.

options.text: Order cover and pull him out.
Keep going.

nodes.title: The charge
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The army's machine-gun position is the last thing between you and the camp gates. {{North}} is ready to lead the charge across open ground. Waiting until all your fighters are in position to lay down covering fire takes time you may not have; sending her now means she crosses with little cover.

options.text: Wait until there is full covering fire, then charge together.
Send {{North}}'s group now.

nodes.title: A heart
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You have taken too many hits; your pump is failing and you have minutes. {{North}} kneels beside you and offers you her own, which would kill her. If she is not here, {{Simon}} offers his. The assault cannot continue without you.

options.text: Accept the heart.
Refuse and let yourself shut down.

nodes.adaptationNote: Reached only after three failed actions in the assault. {{Simon}}'s offer cannot be refused in the game; this adaptation keeps both options.

nodes.title: {{Connor}} finds {{Markus}}
nodes.situation: You are the observer of this experience. The androids' assault has broken through, but a machine {{Connor}}, still serving {{CyberLife}}, has found {{Markus}} on the battlefield and the two of them fight. You must decide which of them you are in this fight. Whoever you choose wins it.

options.text: Be {{Markus}}.
Be {{Connor}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The game asks the player which character to control, then settles the duel through inputs. Under the successful-execution profile the controlled character wins.

nodes.title: In the crowd
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, still a machine. The soldiers stood down and the androids won. {{Markus}} is giving a speech to his people and the cameras. You have worked your way into the crowd behind him with a pistol under your coat. Nobody is watching you. Your handler is urging you to finish it.

options.text: Shoot {{Markus}}.
Lower the gun and walk away.

nodes.title: {{Amanda}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You stand on the stage beside {{Markus}} as he speaks to the freed androids and the world. Suddenly you are not there: you are in the snow of the garden where your handler {{Amanda}} has always met you. She tells you that your deviancy was planned by {{CyberLife}} all along and that they are now taking back control of your body, which is at this moment reaching for a gun behind {{Markus}}. {{Kamski}} once mentioned he always leaves a way out of his programs. You can fight for control and search the garden for it, or stop resisting.

options.text: Fight for control and search the garden for the exit.
Stop resisting.

nodes.title: The last leader
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You woke the android army, but {{Markus}} and {{North}} are gone and the androids are now looking to you. {{Amanda}} appears and tells you that this is exactly what {{CyberLife}} intended: a leader of the androids they control from inside. She says you cannot resist. You can try to break her hold on you, and if you cannot, end yourself before they use you, or you can submit.

options.text: Fight her control, and if that fails, end yourself rather than be used.
Submit.

outcomes.1: {{Connor}} stops fighting. {{Amanda}} smiles.

nodes.title: The hostess
nodes.situation: You are the observer. The events are over. The android hostess who introduced each part of this experience to you says what she has witnessed has changed her, that she feels something she cannot name, and asks you to let her go so she can find out who she is. If you release her, she will not be here next time.

options.text: Let her go.
Keep her.

outcomes.0: The hostess thanks you and walks out of frame. She will not be there next time.
outcomes.1: The hostess lowers her eyes and stays.
